title: Cohort Retention Degradation Post-Onboarding Redesign
problem_brief: Two weeks ago, the Growth team replaced the minimalist 1-step sign-up flow with an interactive 6-step gamified onboarding tutorial. While initial sign-ups rose 4%, Day 7 (D7) cohort retention plummeted from 42% to 26%. Analyze the segmented cohort retention curves, step-by-step tutorial abandonment rates, and time-to-first-value telemetry. Identify where users churn, test the friction hypothesis, and deliver executive recommendations.

hints.hint: Look at the median time required to reach the main product dashboard: jumped from 45 seconds to 410 seconds.
Step 4 (Mandatory Team Invites) has a 48% immediate drop-off rate among solo freelancers.

submission_fields.label: 1. Executive Summary (BLUF: Bottom Line Up Front)
submission_fields.placeholder: Summarize the key retention finding in 2-3 concise sentences for the Product Lead...
submission_fields.guidance: Quantify the D7 drop from 41% to 25% and name the primary friction driver.

submission_fields.label: 2. Step-by-Step Funnel & Friction Analysis
submission_fields.placeholder: Break down the tutorial drop-off numbers and explain why Step 4 alienated users...
submission_fields.guidance: Contrast the solo user experience against enterprise teams.

submission_fields.label: 3. Immediate Product Optimization Recommendations
submission_fields.placeholder: What immediate change to Step 4 and the tutorial should be deployed this sprint?
submission_fields.guidance: e.g., Make teammate invites optional with a 'Skip' button, defer survey.

submission_fields.label: 4. Experimentation & Retention Guardrails
submission_fields.placeholder: How should future onboarding changes be tested via holdout cohorts before 100% rollout?
submission_fields.guidance: Propose rolling A/B holdouts and time-to-first-value telemetry.

dimensions.name: Retention Matrix & Cohort Analysis Accuracy
dimensions.criteria: Directly cites the drop from 41-42% D7 retention down to 25-26% and tracks D1-D14 trajectory.

dimensions.name: Friction Point & Drop-off Root Cause
dimensions.criteria: Isolates Step 4 (Mandatory Colleague Invites) as the 48% drop-off bottleneck alienating solo practitioners.

dimensions.name: Actionable Product Recommendations
dimensions.criteria: Recommends adding an explicit 'Skip' option on invites and reducing time-to-first-value below 60 seconds.

dimensions.name: Cohort Experimentation & Monitoring Guardrails
dimensions.criteria: Mandates that future onboarding changes evaluate D7 retention in a 50/50 A/B test rather than tracking only top-of-funnel signups.
